question.:question/problem: Calculate the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB}$, $\overset{\to }{AC}$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$, given the points $A(9, 6, 1)$, $B(9, 7, 2)$, $C(7, 5, 2)$, and $D(7, 8, 3)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we find the displacement vectors $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ that span the parallelepiped:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(9i+7j+2k)-(9i+6j+k) \\  & =j+k \\  & =⟨0,1,1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(7i+5j+2k)-(9i+6j+k) \\  & =-2i-j+k \\  & =⟨-2,-1,1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AD} & =d-a \\  & =(7i+8j+3k)-(9i+6j+k) \\  & =-2i+2j+2k \\  & =⟨-2,2,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

Computing the triple product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot (\overset{\to }{AC}\times \overset{\to }{AD}) & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1 \\ -2 & -1 & 1 \\ -2 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =0\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}|-1\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}|+1\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =0\cdot ((-1)\cdot 2-2\cdot 1)+(-1)\cdot ((-2)\cdot 2-(-2)\cdot 1)+1\cdot ((-2)\cdot 2-(-2)\cdot (-1)) \\  & =0\cdot ((-2)-2)+(-1)\cdot ((-4)-(-2))+1\cdot ((-4)-2) \\  & =0+2+(-6) \\  & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of the corresponding parallelepiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ is

$$
V=|-4|=4.
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(2i+3j+k)-(i+2j-k) \\  & =i+j+2k \\  & =⟨1,1,2⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(4i+j+2k)-(i+2j-k) \\  & =3i-j+3k \\  & =⟨3,-1,3⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AD} & =d-a \\  & =(i+4j+2k)-(i+2j-k) \\  & =2j+3k \\  & =⟨0,2,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

Computing the triple product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot (\overset{\to }{AC}\times \overset{\to }{AD}) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}|-1\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}|+2\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot ((-1)\cdot 3-2\cdot 3)+(-1)\cdot (3\cdot 3-0\cdot 3)+2\cdot (3\cdot 2-0\cdot (-1)) \\  & =1\cdot ((-3)-6)+(-1)\cdot (9-0)+2\cdot (6-0) \\  & =(-9)+(-9)+12 \\  & =-6.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(3i+4j+k)-(3i+3j-2k) \\  & =j+3k \\  & =⟨0,1,3⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(3i+2j-4k)-(3i+3j-2k) \\  & =-j-2k \\  & =⟨0,-1,-2⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AD} & =d-a \\  & =(7i+5j-3k)-(3i+3j-2k) \\  & =4i+2j-k \\  & =⟨4,2,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

Computing the triple product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot (\overset{\to }{AC}\times \overset{\to }{AD}) & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 \\ 4 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =0\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}|-1\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}|+3\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 4 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =0\cdot ((-1)\cdot (-1)-2\cdot (-2))+(-1)\cdot (0\cdot (-1)-4\cdot (-2))+3\cdot (0\cdot 2-4\cdot (-1)) \\  & =0\cdot (1-(-4))+(-1)\cdot (0-(-8))+3\cdot (0-(-4)) \\  & =0+(-8)+12 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of the corresponding parallelepiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ is

$$
V=|4|=4.

$$

$$

First, we find the displacement vectors $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ that span the parallelepiped:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(-3i-5j-5k)-(2i-3j) \\  & =-5i-2j-5k \\  & =⟨-5,-2,-5⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(-i+j-k)-(2i-3j) \\  & =-3i+4j-k \\  & =⟨-3,4,-1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AD} & =d-a \\  & =(-3i-j-3k)-(2i-3j) \\  & =-5i+2j-3k \\  & =⟨-5,2,-3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

Computing the triple product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot (\overset{\to }{AC}\times \overset{\to }{AD}) & =|\begin{aligned}-5 & -2 & -5 \\ -3 & 4 & -1 \\ -5 & 2 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-5)\cdot |\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}|-(-2)\cdot |\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 \\ -5 & -3\end{aligned}|+(-5)\cdot |\begin{aligned}-3 & 4 \\ -5 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-5)\cdot (4\cdot (-3)-2\cdot (-1))+2\cdot ((-3)\cdot (-3)-(-5)\cdot (-1))+(-5)\cdot ((-3)\cdot 2-(-5)\cdot 4) \\  & =(-5)\cdot ((-12)-(-2))+2\cdot (9-5)+(-5)\cdot ((-6)-(-20)) \\  & =50+8+(-70) \\  & =-12.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of the corresponding parallelepiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ is

$$

Computing the triple product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot (\overset{\to }{AC}\times \overset{\to }{AD}) & =|\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & -1 \\ -2 & -4 & 5 \\ -4 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =4\cdot |\begin{aligned}-4 & 5 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}|-(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 \\ -4 & 0\end{aligned}|+(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & -4 \\ -4 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =4\cdot ((-4)\cdot 0-3\cdot 5)+1\cdot ((-2)\cdot 0-(-4)\cdot 5)+(-1)\cdot ((-2)\cdot 3-(-4)\cdot (-4)) \\  & =4\cdot (0-15)+1\cdot (0-(-20))+(-1)\cdot ((-6)-16) \\  & =(-60)+20+22 \\  & =-18.\end{aligned}

Calculate the volume $V$ of the parallelepiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD},$ given the points $A(2,3,-2),$, $B(6,8,3),$, $C(-1,4,-1),$ and $D(6,8,2).$

$V=${{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we find the displacement vectors $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ that span the parallelepiped:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(6i+8j+3k)-(2i+3j-2k) \\  & =4i+5j+5k \\  & =⟨4,5,5⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(-i+4j-k)-(2i+3j-2k) \\  & =-3i+j+k \\  & =⟨-3,1,1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AD} & =d-a \\  & =(6i+8j+2k)-(2i+3j-2k) \\  & =4i+5j+4k \\  & =⟨4,5,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

Computing the triple product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot (\overset{\to }{AC}\times \overset{\to }{AD}) & =|\begin{aligned}4 & 5 & 5 \\ -3 & 1 & 1 \\ 4 & 5 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =4\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 5 & 4\end{aligned}|-5\cdot |\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ 4 & 4\end{aligned}|+5\cdot |\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ 4 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =4\cdot (1\cdot 4-5\cdot 1)+(-5)\cdot ((-3)\cdot 4-4\cdot 1)+5\cdot ((-3)\cdot 5-4\cdot 1) \\  & =4\cdot (4-5)+(-5)\cdot ((-12)-4)+5\cdot ((-15)-4) \\  & =(-4)+80+(-95) \\  & =-19.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of the corresponding parallelepiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ is

$$
V=|-19|=19.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(-2i+3j-2k)-(-3i-j+3k) \\  & =i+4j-5k \\  & =⟨1,4,-5⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(i-6j+2k)-(-3i-j+3k) \\  & =4i-5j-k \\  & =⟨4,-5,-1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AD} & =d-a \\  & =(-4j)-(-3i-j+3k) \\  & =3i-3j-3k \\  & =⟨3,-3,-3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

Computing the triple product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot (\overset{\to }{AC}\times \overset{\to }{AD}) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -5 \\ 4 & -5 & -1 \\ 3 & -3 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}-5 & -1 \\ -3 & -3\end{aligned}|-4\cdot |\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 3 & -3\end{aligned}|+(-5)\cdot |\begin{aligned}4 & -5 \\ 3 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot ((-5)\cdot (-3)-(-3)\cdot (-1))+(-4)\cdot (4\cdot (-3)-3\cdot (-1))+(-5)\cdot (4\cdot (-3)-3\cdot (-5)) \\  & =1\cdot (15-3)+(-4)\cdot ((-12)-(-3))+(-5)\cdot ((-12)-(-15)) \\  & =12+36+(-15) \\  & =33.\end{aligned}

\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot (\overset{\to }{AC}\times \overset{\to }{AD}) & =|\begin{aligned}-2 & -5 & -4 \\ 5 & -2 & 4 \\ -2 & -1 & -4\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-2)\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 \\ -1 & -4\end{aligned}|-(-5)\cdot |\begin{aligned}5 & 4 \\ -2 & -4\end{aligned}|+(-4)\cdot |\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-2)\cdot ((-2)\cdot (-4)-(-1)\cdot 4)+5\cdot (5\cdot (-4)-(-2)\cdot 4)+(-4)\cdot (5\cdot (-1)-(-2)\cdot (-2)) \\  & =(-2)\cdot (8-(-4))+5\cdot ((-20)-(-8))+(-4)\cdot ((-5)-4) \\  & =(-24)+(-60)+36 \\  & =-48.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of the corresponding parallelepiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ is

$$
V=|-48|=48.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Calculate the volume $V$ of the parallelepiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD},$ given the points $A(3,0,2),$, $B(7,-4,1),$, $C(4,1,6),$ and $D(8,-5,3).$

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we find the displacement vectors $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ that span the parallelepiped:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(7i-4j+k)-(3i+2k) \\  & =4i-4j-k \\  & =⟨4,-4,-1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(4i+j+6k)-(3i+2k) \\  & =i+j+4k \\  & =⟨1,1,4⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AD} & =d-a \\  & =(8i-5j+3k)-(3i+2k) \\  & =5i-5j+k \\  & =⟨5,-5,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

Computing the triple product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot (\overset{\to }{AC}\times \overset{\to }{AD}) & =|\begin{aligned}4 & -4 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 4 \\ 5 & -5 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =4\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ -5 & 1\end{aligned}|-(-4)\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}|+(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 5 & -5\end{aligned}| \\  & =4\cdot (1\cdot 1-(-5)\cdot 4)+4\cdot (1\cdot 1-5\cdot 4)+(-1)\cdot (1\cdot (-5)-5\cdot 1) \\  & =4\cdot (1-(-20))+4\cdot (1-20)+(-1)\cdot ((-5)-5) \\  & =84+(-76)+10 \\  & =18.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of the corresponding parallelepiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ is

$$
V=|18|=18.
$$
